summary: In 2026, the canonical model-optimization sequence is prompt engineering first, then RAG when the system needs fresh or proprietary knowledge, and fine-tuning only when behavior remains inconsistent at scale after the cheaper options provably hit a wall. Base models (Qwen3, Llama 4, Gemma 3) are now strong enough out of the box that the bar for needing fine-tuning keeps rising, so it is best reserved for baking in consistent style, format, or task-specific skills. Fine-tuning changes how the model behaves by default, while RAG changes what it knows and prompting changes how you ask.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning only after prompt engineering and RAG provably fail to produce consistent behavior at scale.
Use it when you need to bake a specific style, tone, output format, or task-specific skill into the model's weights rather than injecting knowledge at query time.
Prefer fine-tuning over RAG when the problem is behavioral consistency or latency/cost optimization, not missing or changing facts.
Fine-tune when you have a high-quality, representative labeled dataset and the task is stable enough to justify the training and maintenance cost.

tools.name: OpenAI Fine-Tuning API
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token for training plus higher inference rates on tuned models; supervised, DPO, and RFT options billed per 1M tokens (varies by base model).
tools.best_for: Instruction tuning and behavior/format adaptation for teams already on the OpenAI stack wanting zero infra overhead.

tools.name: Hugging Face AutoTrain
tools.pricing_paid: Pay for compute via chosen GPU hardware (T4/A100/H100) on HF infrastructure; Inference Endpoints billed hourly by instance.
features: Full LoRA, QLoRA, and DPO support via Transformers
tools.best_for: Research and experimentation plus no-code domain adaptation across the widest range of open models.

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source and free; Pro/Enterprise tiers for multi-GPU and managed support.
features: Runs 20B QLoRA on a single RTX 4090
tools.best_for: Fast, memory-efficient fine-tuning on consumer or single-GPU hardware.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Fine-Tuning
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per token for custom training jobs plus provisioned throughput hourly charges for hosting the custom model.
tools.best_for: Enterprise domain adaptation within an AWS-governed, compliance-sensitive environment.

tools.name: Vertex AI (Google Cloud)
tools.pricing_paid: Pay per node-hour / per-token training plus deployment cost; tuned Gemini models billed at inference.
supported_models: select open models via Model Garden
tools.best_for: Enterprise instruction tuning and distillation for teams on Google Cloud.

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; compute cost on your own or rented GPUs.
features: Supports nearly every fine-tuning method (LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, full FT)
tools.best_for: Flexible, reproducible, configuration-driven fine-tuning for multi-GPU setups and advanced methods.

tools.name: LLaMA-Factory
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; compute cost on your own or rented GPUs.
tools.best_for: Easiest entry point for teams wanting a web UI and the widest set of tuning methods including RLHF variants.

tools.name: Together AI
tools.pricing_paid: Fine-tuning priced per 1M tokens: $0.48 (LoRA up to 16B) to $8.00 (full FT 70-100B); specialized models $5-$40/1M tokens plus a minimum job charge; storage $0.16/GiB/month.
tools.best_for: Production fine-tuning plus ultra-low-latency serving of open models at scale.

tools.name: Replicate
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-second GPU billing for training; deployed models billed per run/second of compute.
tools.best_for: Quick API-driven fine-tuning and instant deployment for developers and small teams.

tools.name: Modal
tools.pricing_paid: Serverless pay-per-second GPU pricing (A100/H100); free monthly compute credits for new users.
supported_models: Any open model (bring-your-own code with Axolotl/Unsloth/TRL)
tools.best_for: Infrastructure-flexible, serverless fine-tuning where you control the training code but not the hardware.

tools.name: TRL (Transformer Reinforcement Learning)
tools.pricing_paid: Free open-source; compute cost on your own or rented GPUs.
tools.best_for: RLHF and preference-optimization research/production where fine-grained control over the training loop is needed.
